instruction: deps.txt holds dependency edges 'A B' (A depends on B, one per line). Write order.py printing a valid build order (dependencies before dependents), one node per line; if a cycle exists print 'CYCLE' instead. Any valid order is accepted. Run it.
setup:
printf 'web api
api db
worker db
web worker
' > deps.txt

grader.script:
python3 order.py > got.txt && python3 -c "
lines = open('got.txt').read().split()
assert lines != ['CYCLE']
edges = [('web','api'),('api','db'),('worker','db'),('web','worker')]
pos = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(lines)}
assert set(lines) == {'web','api','worker','db'}, 'node set wrong'
assert all(pos[b] < pos[a] for a, b in edges), 'dependency after dependent'
" && printf 'a b\nb a\n' > deps.txt && python3 order.py | grep -qx 'CYCLE'

oracle.script:
cat > order.py <<'EOF'
edges = [ln.split() for ln in open('deps.txt') if ln.split()]
nodes = set()
for a, b in edges:
    nodes.add(a)
    nodes.add(b)
deps = {n: set() for n in nodes}
for a, b in edges:
    deps[a].add(b)
out, temp, perm, cyc = [], set(), set(), []
def visit(n):
    if cyc or n in perm:
        return
    if n in temp:
        cyc.append(True)
        return
    temp.add(n)
    for d in sorted(deps[n]):
        visit(d)
    temp.discard(n)
    perm.add(n)
    out.append(n)
for n in sorted(nodes):
    visit(n)
print('CYCLE' if cyc else '\n'.join(out))
EOF
python3 order.py
